problem: The first v3 retrain completed only 150 gradient updates in 3 hours and the policy degraded (grasp 0.20 -> 0.00) with critic_loss still diverging (0.15 -> 8.39). The obvious reading -- 'the fixes made it worse' -- is wrong; the run never had enough optimiser steps to fit a freshly initialised critic.

measurement.where_the_time_goes: Each chunk decision costs 30 actions x 2 sim substeps = 60 simulator steps plus a VLM forward. At 479 ms per env step the run collected only 376 chunk decisions in 3 hours, which at UTD 0.5 yields ~188 updates.
measurement.the_original_run_for_comparison: The 415k RLPD checkpoint reached 2983 updates by running ~415k env steps (roughly 50 hours) at the SAME UTD 0.5 -- not by being more efficient per step.

measured_optimiser_cost.note: VLM features are cached in the replay buffer, so an update does not re-run the VLM.

conclusion: The bottleneck is simulation and VLM rollout throughput, not the optimiser. Raising the update-to-data ratio buys gradient updates at ~0.1% wall-clock overhead. UTD 8 reaches the original run's 2983 updates within a single 3-hour budget.
caveat: High UTD on a small replay buffer risks overfitting the critic to limited data -- the standard reason UTD is kept low. Two things mitigate it here: RLPD fills half of every batch from the 22-episode demonstration buffer, and the DCT basis cut the critic's input from 900 to 180 dimensions, raising transitions-per-input-dimension from 8.2 to 41. The run must still be watched for critic divergence, which is why critic_loss is a reported readout.

CORRECTION_after_run_2.what_was_projected: This contract projected that raising UTD to 8 would cost ~13 s over a 3-hour run (0.12% overhead) and yield ~3000 gradient updates, based on a measured critic update of 4.66 ms.
CORRECTION_after_run_2.why_the_projection_was_wrong: The 4.66 ms timing measured ONLY the critic MLP. It excluded demo_batch, where a cache MISS runs two vlm_encode calls. A direct measurement puts vlm_encode at 107.5 ms, so a miss costs 215 ms. RLPD draws BATCH*DEMO_FRAC = 4 demo transitions per update, so at UTD 8 the loop can pay up to 8 x 4 x 2 = 64 encodes per environment decision while the cache fills. Benchmarking a component and presenting it as the system cost is the error.
CORRECTION_after_run_2.second_cost_found: The step-0 evaluations (init and init_stochastic) run 2 x N_EVAL_PERIODIC x EP_CHUNKS = 1150 chunk rollouts BEFORE any gradient step. For both runs that is the single largest block of work, and it duplicates a v3 baseline already scored under the same predicate.

fixes.PREWARM_DEMO_CACHE: Encode every demonstration transition once before training: 489 transitions x 2 encodes x 107.5 ms = ~105 s, one time. After that demo_batch is a dict lookup and UTD scales on MLP cost as originally intended.
fixes.RUN_INIT_EVAL: Allows skipping the step-0 evaluations when the warm-start checkpoint has already been scored under the same predicate, freeing ~1150 chunk rollouts.

CORRECTION_after_run_2.method_note: Two throughput projections in this project have now been wrong in the same way -- extrapolating from a measured piece rather than the measured whole. Any future throughput claim should be validated by a short end-to-end run before a long one is launched.
